title: Vite vs esbuild vs tsup
deck: Cold production builds of a TypeScript library — ESM, minified, no declarations.

verdict.headline: esbuild finished in 12 ms; the nearest contender took 185 ms
verdict.summary: esbuild built zod in 12.3 ms at the median. tsup took 184.8 ms; Vite took 232.7 ms. esbuild and tsup produced identical 59 KB bundles; Vite's Rollup-based pipeline emitted 86 KB.

limitations: Cold builds only. No watch mode, incremental rebuilds, or hot module replacement timing.
One corpus: a zero-dependency TypeScript library (zod 3.24.4, 13 files, ~6,600 lines). Application builds with many dependencies, code-splitting, or CSS processing may produce different rankings.
Build speed says nothing about dev-server experience, plugin ecosystems, or output correctness beyond "it built."
All three tools use esbuild's minifier. Vite delegates bundling to Rollup, then minification to esbuild; tsup wraps esbuild for both steps. The minification overhead is the same across candidates.
Declaration file generation (.d.ts) is disabled for all candidates. Enabling tsup's dts option invokes the TypeScript compiler and would add significant time.
Vite's larger output (86 KB vs. 59 KB) reflects Rollup's bundling strategy, not a minification difference. Both outputs are functionally equivalent.
